title: Japan’s economy unexpectedly shrinks as inflation squeezes households
html:
The first contraction in four quarters underscores the uneven nature of Japan’s economic recovery.

PHOTO: UNSPLASH

AI generated

TOKYO – Japan’s economy unexpectedly contracted an annualised 0.1% in the July-September quarter, government data showed on Nov 16, reflecting weak consumer spending as households grappled with higher living costs.

The first contraction in four quarters underscores the uneven nature of Japan’s economic recovery, with households remaining vulnerable to persistent inflation despite rising wages.

Still, policymakers are unlikely to view the weakness as a brake on Japan’s moderate recovery, with resilient corporate activity, rising real wages and robust demand for artificial intelligence-related investment underpinning growth.

“While growth was indeed negative this time, there is no need to be overly pessimistic about the result,” said Kento Minami, senior economist at Daiwa Securities. “My impression is that moderate growth is probably continuing.”

Minami also said the results are unlikely to derail the Bank of Japan’s (BOJ’s) tightening path, as the central bank remains focused on inflation risks, adding that firm domestic price pressures and a global backdrop of higher interest rates leave little room for a dovish policy shift.

The gross domestic product data compared with a median market forecast of 0.3% annualised growth in a Reuters poll, and followed a revised 1.7% expansion in the previous quarter.

The reading translated into a quarterly fall of 0.02%, compared with the median estimate of a 0.1% increase.

Private consumption, which accounts for more than half of economic output, fell 0.3%, compared with a market estimate of a 0.2% decline.

Household spending was hurt by persistent price pressures and poor weather, including heavy rain and typhoons during the quarter.

Demand for automobiles and air conditioners retreated following the temporary boost in the previous quarter from tax and regulatory changes.

“Strong wage growth should support consumption, but higher prices linked to Middle East tensions will continue to squeeze household purchasing power,” said Masato Koike, senior ⁠economist at Sompo Institute Plus.

Capital spending, a key driver of private demand, rose 1.6%, versus a market forecast for a 1.5% increase, backed by investment in labour-saving technologies and artificial intelligence-related projects.

Net external demand, or exports minus imports, knocked 0.6 percentage point off growth, compared with a market forecast for a 0.4 percentage point drag on gross domestic product growth.

Imports rose sharply as oil and other energy purchases recovered after Japan diversified procurement following disruptions linked to the war in the Middle East.

The BOJ will closely scrutinise the latest data as it assesses whether the economy can withstand further interest-rate increases.

With stubbornly high energy costs and rising import prices from a weak yen adding to inflationary pressures, the BOJ has stepped up its policy tightening in 2026, delivering interest rate hikes in June and September.

Many analysts expect the next BOJ rate hike as soon as December.

A monthly survey of 37 economists by the Japan Center for Economic Research showed the economy is expected to grow 0.89% in fiscal 2026 and 1.02% in fiscal 2027, suggesting economists see growth remaining modest but resilient.

Japan’s longer-term growth challenges remain in focus, with the International Monetary Fund projecting the country will slip to the world’s sixth-largest economy in nominal dollar terms in 2027 in dollar terms, overtaken by India and Britain.

Japan is currently the world’s fourth-largest after Germany. REUTERS
summary: Private consumption, which accounts for more than half of economic output, fell 0.3%.
